{{Wireless adapter |brand=Alpha Networks |model=WUS-G09V |revision= |upc= |ean= |asin= |price= |est_release_date= |fcc_date=09/26/2006 |manuf_country=Taiwan |manuf= |manuf_model= |manuf_rev= |availability= |if=USB (non-standard connector) |if_bus_version=2.0 |vendor_id= |device_id= |subvendor_id= |subdevice_id= |fcc_id=RRK2005070154-1 |ic_id= |chip1_brand=Conexant |chip1_model=CX3889 |chip2_brand=Intersil |chip2_model=ISL3686B |chip3_brand= |chip3_model= |flags= |ant_conn=U.FL |802dot11_protocols=bg |txchains= |rxchains= |sstreams= |oui= |lin_driver= |win_driver= }} "8WUSG09V.0A1G" is silkscreened on the board in the FCC photos.
A MAC address (the MAC has a 00:11:95 OUI) is affixed to the back of the board in the FCC photos. :The FCC EUT's label also has a MAC on it (w/ a 00:17:9A OUI).
The FCC manual indicates that this device uses ISL3889 ([http://pccomponents.com/datasheets/CONEX06-1961BRO_PROD_CATALOG.PDF presumably CX3889]). :It is also specified as using CX3510 (PA).
The FCC test report list the following as covered models... *Alpha Networks WUS-G09V *Alpha Networks WUS-G09PB *Penbex WUGC-100 ('''Penbex''' apparently sold internet radios) *Verifone WUS-G09V
